_readme: SHIP DESIGN RULES — the two things that make a fleet read as a fleet.
1. CIVILIZATION IDENTITY, BUT ALWAYS A STARSHIP.
Each civ has a strong aesthetic drawn from its biology (Species.cs), and each one carries a
`techMandate` that exists to stop the aesthetic eating the ship. Left alone, 'Aquarii' returns a
fish and 'Sylvan' returns a tree — the first pass produced a literal jellyfish for a deep-space
station and a naval aircraft carrier for the Terran carrier. The mandate is the counterweight:
sea forms yes, but with obvious engineering — thrusters, sensors, weapon mounts, panel lines.
2. LINEAGE. A Mk II must read as the SAME SHIP as the Mk I, refitted — not a different design that
happens to share a name. That is a visual promise the UI already makes by calling them Mk I/II/III,
and it is what makes an upgrade feel earned.
Mechanically this is why generation is ORDERED. Each tier's concept art is generated as an
image-to-image edit of the tier below it, so the hull, proportions, camera angle and palette carry
forward and only the `upgrade` text changes. Generating all three from text independently gives
three unrelated ships every time, no matter how carefully the prompts are worded.
`chain: true` lineages inherit tier to tier. `chain: false` are one-offs with no ancestor.
referenceStrength is how strongly the previous tier's art constrains the next: high enough that the
ship is recognisably the same, low enough that the added armour and guns actually appear.
_tailNotes: The tail is not decoration — every clause in it is load-bearing downstream.
ORIENTATION: the bow/stern and dorsal/ventral clauses exist so ShipMeshManifest's bounds heuristic
lands. It infers forward from the longest axis, up from the shortest, and the stern from whichever
half carries more geometry — so a hull that is longer than it is wide, wider than it is tall, with
its mass and engines aft and its detail on top, auto-orients correctly on import. A blobby or
symmetric concept produces a mesh that flies sideways and needs a hand-written manifest line.
LIVERY PLACEMENT: the primary has to land on large contiguous panels and the secondary on small
separate trim, or extract-color-masks.mjs cannot tell them apart in the baked albedo and the ship
can never take a player's colours. Naming the SURFACES rather than a percentage is what finally
worked — Meshy ignores proportions but follows 'along the flanks' and 'on the fin edges'.
DETAIL: panel lines and greebling give the albedo luminance variance, which is also what the
verifier measures to tell a real texture from a flat fill.
sharedTail: Bow distinct from stern; longer than wide, wider than tall; engines aft, sensors forward; flat ventral, detail dorsal. STRONG SATURATED COLOUR, never white or pale. Bold primary panels on flanks and spine; secondary only on small trim and lights. Dense panel lines, rivets, weathering. One ship, plain black background, three-quarter view, no text.
stationTail: A built orbital structure, radially symmetric, no bow, no engines. STRONG SATURATED COLOUR, never white or pale. Bold primary panels on the main hull; secondary only on small trim and docking lights. Dense panel lines, rivets, weathering. One structure, plain black background, three-quarter view, no text.

Terran.aesthetic: steel grey-blue gunmetal plating, structural ribs, angular panels, black radiator fins
Terran.techMandate: riveted modular build, visible thrusters, sensor masts, weapon mounts; never organic

Aquarii.aesthetic: a CYBORG SEA CREATURE starship - shark, whale, manta ray, crab, anglerfish or jellyfish body with deep sea-teal scaled skin, fins and cartilage
Aquarii.techMandate: half creature half machine: metal armour plates bolted over the living body, mechanical gill vents, cybernetic lens eyes, cable bundles, glowing implant seams, thruster pods grafted to the tail

Pyrothian.aesthetic: dark charcoal basalt armour, overlapping ablative plate, brass heat fins, magma seams
Pyrothian.techMandate: heavy machinery: bolted plate, cooling pipework, huge engine bells, gun barrels; never a bare rock

Cryithn.aesthetic: deep glacier-blue faceted armour over frosted silver alloy, rime-crusted plating
Cryithn.techMandate: precise machined build: crisp seams, sensor spines, recessed weapon ports, drive nozzles; never natural ice

Sylvan.aesthetic: deep forest-green living hull, woven vine over a seed-pod shell, dark bark plating
Sylvan.techMandate: GROWN BUT ENGINEERED: metal fittings, sensor pods, engine nozzles and gun mounts grafted in; never a plant

lineages.family: a small fast survey craft — slim dart hull, oversized sensor dish, single dominant engine

tiers.upgrade: the baseline model: minimal armour, one engine, one dish
the SAME ship refitted: hull lengthened, a second engine added alongside the first, a second sensor mast, light armour plate over the nose, more antennae
the SAME ship at its final refit: three engines, a faired sensor spine along the dorsal line, sleeker swept armour, additional dishes and a small defensive turret

lineages.family: a mobile laboratory — slender hull with sensor booms, dish arrays and observation blisters

tiers.upgrade: the baseline model: one dish boom, a few blisters
the SAME ship refitted: longer hull, twin dish booms, a dorsal telescope array, more observation blisters
the SAME ship at its final refit: a rotating instrument ring amidships, a large forward scanning lens, dense antenna clusters
the flagship of this line: everything above, larger, crowned with a great sensor ring and radio dishes

lineages.family: a compact agile warship — arrowhead hull, forward gun barrels, stubby swept wings

tiers.upgrade: the baseline model: two gun barrels, thin armour, small wings
the SAME fighter refitted: four gun barrels, armoured shoulder plating over the cockpit, broader wings, missile rails added under them
the SAME fighter at its final refit: underslung cannon pods, heavy layered armour, longer swept wings, extra thrusters and a sensor blister

lineages.family: a warship of the battle line — armoured hull, turret batteries, heavy engines

tiers.upgrade: the smallest of the line: lean armoured hull, turret blisters, missile racks
the same design language scaled up: thicker armour belt, multiple turret batteries along the spine
the same family as a fleet carrier: long flat-topped hull, open flight deck, strike-craft launch bays along the flanks. STILL A SPACESHIP, never an ocean-going aircraft carrier
the same family at its heaviest: colossal slab-armoured hull, an immense spinal cannon, layered gun batteries, enormous engine bank

lineages.family: a long-range pathfinder — lean endurance hull, enormous fuel tanks, wide sensor prow

tiers.upgrade: built for reach above all else

lineages.family: a tiny expendable deep-space probe — small instrument core, solar collector, whip antenna

tiers.upgrade: cheap, unmanned, barely more than an instrument package

lineages.family: a huge slow settler vessel — fat cargo-heavy hull carrying prefabricated habitat modules and a landing pod

tiers.upgrade: built to be spent: it lands once and becomes a city

lineages.family: a civilian mining barge — blunt industrial hull, ore hoppers, cutting arms, refinery drum

tiers.upgrade: working machinery, unglamorous and heavy

lineages.family: a civilian freight hauler — long spine strung with modular cargo containers behind a small bridge

tiers.upgrade: all capacity, no armament

lineages.family: a vast climate-engineering vessel — industrial hull dominated by atmosphere-processor nozzles and cooling towers

tiers.upgrade: a factory that flies

lineages.family: an orbital structure — not a ship, no bow and no engines; radially symmetric, built to sit still

tiers.upgrade: a rudimentary armoured drum ringed with heavy gun turrets and missile silos
the same construction style as a laboratory: habitat torus, dish arrays, telescopes, lit lab windows
the same construction style as a comms relay: a slender mast carrying a huge parabolic dish and antenna clusters
the same construction style as a depot: fuel spheres and cargo drums around a docking spine
a large complex combining all of the above: stacked habitat rings, dishes, docking arms, defensive turrets
a colossal ring of atmosphere-processor nozzles around a reactor core
a compact self-sufficient core inside an open lattice tower wrapped in enormous solar collector wings. A BUILT STATION, never a creature. TALL and VERTICAL, not a dome and not a disc
an orbital city the size of a small moon: vast nested habitat rings, spires, docking bays, a glowing reactor heart
a colossal OPEN five-armed gate — arcing emitter arms curling inward around a blazing aperture. NOT a closed ring, NOT a dome, NOT a reef: open space between the arms

techProgression.1: EARLY AND SIMPLE: bare hull, one small engine, one or two light weapons, a couple of small lights. Uncluttered.
techProgression.2: IMPROVED: light armour plates over the vitals, two engines, several weapon mounts, more lit panels and antennae.
techProgression.3: ADVANCED: layered armour, three engines, multiple weapon mounts and missile rails, dense greebling, many glowing strips.
techProgression.4: HIGH-TECH: heavy segmented armour, a cluster of engines, many weapon systems, glowing energy conduits threaded through the hull.
techProgression.5: THE PINNACLE: colossal layered armour, a whole bank of engines, weapon batteries over every surface, blazing energy cores and light everywhere.
